title: Build a UPGMA tree and correct a distance
instructions:
## Four sequences, one tree

Pairwise distances between four sequences A, B, C and D (rows and columns in that order) are in matrix A of the Matrix tool:

| | A | B | C | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 0 | 2 | 6 | 10 |
| B | 2 | 0 | 6 | 10 |
| C | 6 | 6 | 0 | 10 |
| D | 10 | 10 | 10 | 0 |

**UPGMA** repeatedly joins the closest pair, places their common ancestor at height d/2, and replaces the pair by a cluster whose distance to every other cluster is the average over all members.

## Do this

1. Which pair is joined first? Type the two letters.
2. The height of their ancestor node.
3. The distance from the new cluster to C.
4. The height of the node that joins C.
5. The height of the root.
6. Raw p-distances underestimate change because sites can mutate twice. The **Jukes-Cantor** correction is d = −¾ ln(1 − 4p/3). Correct p = 0.3.

realityNote: UPGMA assumes a molecular clock, so every leaf ends at the same height. When rates differ between lineages it builds the wrong tree, which is why neighbour joining and likelihood methods replaced it for real data.
